doc.title: A visitor can open a public template page, change its inputs, see it recalculate in the browser, and print it, with no account

blocks.title: Problem and motivation
blocks.body:
As of 2026-11-10, the only way anyone sees a CalcTree calculation is inside the authenticated editor. The marketing site can describe a template but cannot let a prospect use one, and there is no URL an engineer can send a client that says "here is the calc, put your numbers in". A public, printable template page is a top-of-funnel asset (linkable from calctree.com, one page per template). The product ask came on 2026-09-09.

The tempting wrong fix is a marketing-site page built on the static editor that calls the production API with an embedded API key. It works for one demo and cannot ship: any authenticated credential can read any calculation by id (CTP-5328), and nothing in the stack gives an anonymous caller a narrower credential.

blocks.title: A public page is one built-in template version that staff explicitly mark public under a slug. A built-in is never public by default.
blocks.body: Adam stated the ownership model on 2026-11-09: a public template page belongs to no workspace or user, visitors cannot change what is stored, and only a CalcTree admin can change it. Built-in templates already match that model and have versions. On 2026-11-10 Adam leaned to this option and said that a public page being a built-in is fine, but not every built-in should become a public page. Rejected: **every eligible built-in becomes public automatically** (Adam, 2026-11-10). Rejected: **a new "public page" entity** (no reuse of authoring, versions or snapshots). Rejected: **paying workspaces publish their own calcs, with the publisher paying for print** (Tim's review on ai-plans#8): it conflicts with the ownership model above. Do not reopen without new evidence. **Reopened on 2026-11-13: Decision 16 supersedes this decision for Milestone B.** Milestone A still publishes one built-in version by hand, as written here.

blocks.title: Evaluation runs only in the visitor's browser, through `runTemplatePreviewInBrowser` over the statements in the version's MDX. Nothing calls the calculations service at visit time.
blocks.body: The browser engine runs the same core as the server, and the frontend#4318 spike ran MathJS and Python anonymously. `simpleCalculate` refuses built-ins anyway (Ground truths). Rejected: **server evaluation through `simpleCalculate` on each input change** (the ai-plans#8 design): it refuses built-ins, needs an anonymous credential, and costs Lambda time on every input change. Rejected: **browser first with server fallback** (the in-app placed-instance model): an anonymous visitor has no server to fall back to. Rejected: **serving the statements at the pinned revision with the MDX** (dpnova's proposed shape on ai-plans#8, 2026-11-06): the browser already builds its statements from the MDX, as the in-app template preview does, so the revision adds nothing at visit time. It is read once at publish for the parity check, which catches any divergence. Do not reopen without new evidence.

blocks.title: Page content reaches the visitor as static files written at publish time to public storage behind a CDN. The visitor's browser never calls a CalcTree API.
blocks.body: No anonymous read path exists as of 2026-11-10, and this choice adds none. Unpublish deletes the files. Adam chose this on 2026-11-10. Rejected: **an anonymous read endpoint in pages** (a live surface with a shield exception, rate limits and caching to maintain). Rejected: **an API key in the page** (any credential reads any calculation by id: CTP-5328). Do not reopen without new evidence.

blocks.title: Publishing is gated, and the gate stores the values.
blocks.body: The staff member's browser runs the version's MDX at its default inputs. Publishing is refused when the MDX brings files (including uploaded images), when the run reports `needsServer: true` or any statement error, or when the browser values differ from the server's stored values at the pinned `(calculationId, revisionId)`. The values from that run are stored with the page and shown before the visitor's engine starts. This answers Tim's point that browser-only execution loses the runtime comparison against the server. Rejected: **no parity check** (a browser engine bug would show a prospect a wrong number with no signal). Rejected: **comparing on every visit** (needs a server call).

blocks.title: In v1 a visitor changes input values only, on the template-page renderer. Full local editing is a later phase, designed for but not built.
blocks.body: Adam chose this on 2026-11-10. An input is what the existing rule finds: a MathJS statement that references nothing, or a math block of literal assignments. The visitor edits it in a parameter field, a math-block line, a `ctselect` picker or an input-table cell (Ground truths). Prose, derived formulas and Python code stay as published (Decision 10). Staff do not narrow the inputs in v1. In the later phase, uploads are no-ops (Adam, 2026-11-09: a resource upload on a public page is skipped). Rejected for v1: **full local editing**, because the production editor mount needs a user (`frontend/packages/editor/src/components/EditorProviders/EditorProviders.tsx:90-96`), YJS readiness (`frontend/packages/editor/src/components/Editor/Editor.tsx:338-346`) and the Dexie action queue for statement edits (`frontend/packages/calculations/src/useStatement/utils.ts:4,69`). Only the browser-test fixtures run an editable editor without them (`frontend/apps/editor-web/browser-tests/block-void-keyboard-fixture.tsx:130-207`).

blocks.title: Print uses the client iframe path (`generatePageHtml` and `createPrintIframe`), called directly from the public page.
blocks.body: It prints what the visitor sees. Rejected: **Gutenberg, called as the publisher** (Tim's review): Gutenberg reads values only from the stored calculation, so it would print the template's stored values, not the visitor's, and it would need a staff credential on a server path. Do not reopen without a way to send Gutenberg trusted values.

blocks.title: Datasets, page files and uploaded images are out of v1, and visitors never bring data.
blocks.body: Publishing refuses versions with `<Dataset>` or `<PageFiles>`. An uploaded image is a page file and also loses its file link in template MDX (CTP-4228), so it is refused the same way. A visitor has no upload, so a visitor never has a dataset. Adam chose this for datasets on 2026-11-10. The later paths for images and datasets are under Deferred.

blocks.title: The public page is its own entry point, outside the app shell, and it never imports the `@calctree/editor` root.
blocks.body: `main.tsx` opens Dexie, the root route mounts Apollo and Customer.io, and importing the `@calctree/editor` root starts PostHog with a cookie (Ground truths). Rejected: **a route under `__root`** (it would load all of that for an anonymous visitor).

blocks.title: A visitor's value is a MathJS expression over the template's own variables, and the input list never changes.
blocks.body: The public page has no host page, so every name in a value refers to the template's own variable: `span = load * 2` makes `span` follow `load`. A circular reference stops the whole run and returns no values (Ground truths), so the page refuses that value at its input and keeps the last good values. The unit check runs on the computed value. The input list comes from the published MDX through `derivePageInputsFromDeclaredStatements`, never from the statements after the visitor's values are applied, so a field never locks. "Reset to published values" clears the map. Agreed with Adam on 2026-11-10. Rejected: **plain values only, refusing names**. Nothing locks either way, so refusing names buys nothing beyond a simpler unit check.

blocks.title: In v1, Python code and derived formulas are read-only, and the wish to edit them becomes the call to action.
blocks.body: Python cells show their code, and their outputs recalculate from the MathJS inputs. Clicking a Python cell or a derived formula shows "Edit the formulas and code in CalcTree", which opens signup, or a guest-activation session once that exists. The click is recorded, so the count decides whether Python code editing is built next. Every constant stays an input (the rule in Decision 5); staff pick the launch templates and check each one before publishing. Agreed with Adam on 2026-11-10 as the lean v1 with the best UX. Rejected for v1: **Python code editing**. The engine part is small, but the edge cases (a script that cannot be stopped once running, imports the browser lacks, slow first package downloads, errors a stranger can read) carry the risk, and it is unknown whether visitors want it. Rejected for v1: **staff narrow the editable inputs at publish**. Add it only if a launch template shows the problem. Both are under Deferred with their trigger.

blocks.title: The public page runs Python in a dedicated Worker and stops a runaway script by restarting it.
blocks.body: A running script cannot be interrupted, and a dedicated Worker, unlike a SharedWorker, can be terminated (Ground truths). An input such as a large loop count could otherwise hang the visitor's Python for the rest of the visit. dpnova's spike also saw the SharedWorker fail to start in one embedded browser while a dedicated Worker worked, and a visitor from a marketing link rarely has several tabs to share a worker between. Rejected: **a SharedWorker with a fallback to a dedicated Worker** (keeps the runaway risk).

blocks.title: On every input change, a MathJS-only run goes first, then the full run.
blocks.body: With any Python in the template, a full run waits for the whole Python start, which dpnova's spike measured at about 23 s on every load (the Step 0 spike measured 10-12 s on current `main`), and a MathJS-only run never calls the worker (Ground truths). Values from the MathJS-only run show at once. A statement that fails in it keeps its previous value with a computing state until the full run returns, because a MathJS statement that reads a Python output fails there as an undefined name. A real MathJS error therefore shows once the full run returns. Rejected: **full run only** (every visit waits 10 s or more before any input has an effect).

blocks.title: The public page is a path on the app host: `/t/<slug>`, with data at `/public-templates/<slug>/page.json`, on the existing editor-web CloudFront distribution.
blocks.body: Adam chose this on 2026-11-11. Its distribution already has the CSP Pyodide needs and serves the `ctpyeng` wheel at its root, and `page.json` fetches stay same-origin. Rejected: **a dedicated subdomain** and **the marketing domain through a proxy**: each needs its own distribution, the wheel served there too, and CORS.

blocks.title: Analytics on the public page is PostHog with `persistence: 'memory'`.
blocks.body: No cookie and no identity across visits. The public entry starts PostHog itself, never through the `@calctree/editor` root. Adam chose this on 2026-11-11. The edit-prompt click count (Decision 10) needs it. Rejected: **no analytics** (leaves the Python editing trigger without data) and **PostHog with a consent banner**.

blocks.title: Step 0 is a go, with a size target added for real networks.
blocks.body: Adam, 2026-11-11, on the frontend#4343 results. All three engines met the criteria as written on localhost. On a 10 Mbit/s link the stored values took 2.2 s, so the plan adds Step 2b to shrink the entry. Before the link goes on the marketing site, stored values must show within 2 s of navigation on a 10 Mbit/s link with 50 ms RTT in Chromium. The smaller Python start (plan Step 1 (iii)) is not built, because removing the micropip list cut the start by only 23-30%. The WebKit stall (Assumptions) is a risk, checked in real Safari before the link goes public, not a blocker.

blocks.title: Template sharing works like sharing a Claude artifact.
blocks.body: Adam decided this in a meeting on 2026-11-13, with these answers on the same day. The shared thing is a template version. The template's author (`workspace_templates.created_by`) or a workspace Admin sets who can open its share link: only them, anyone in the workspace, or anyone with the link. Other members and Viewers cannot change it. Staff do the same for built-ins with `can-manage-builtin-templates`. The link stays the same when the level changes. Only Claude's sharing is copied, in the CalcTree theme: the share dialog, the viewer page header, the no-access page and the list of shared items. Claude's comments, invitations by name or email, export tab and chat are not copied. "Anyone with the link" keeps Decisions 2 to 4: a static `page.json`, written only after the publish gate passes in the browser of the person who shares. "Anyone in the workspace" and "only you" are served by the app to signed-in users and write nothing to public storage. Workspace roles are Admin, Member and Viewer (`rudi/services/rudi/src/schema.graphql:588-592`); there is no Owner role. This decision reverses the rejection in Decision 1 of workspaces publishing their own calculations.

blocks.title: Launch set
blocks.body: Which built-in templates go public first. A candidate needs no uploaded image (CTP-4228), no dataset, and no Excel or `calcSource`. `template_applied` counts can rank candidates.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: one template with MathJS inputs, at least one Python statement and a plot, so the first link exercises every v1 path.

blocks.title: Gallery visibility
blocks.body: Every built-in syncs to every workspace, so a public page is also an in-app template. Until this is decided, share-model does not sync built-in share rows and adds a staff-only query.
blocks.options: Accept it, or hide some public pages from the in-app gallery.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: accept it for v1, because staff already curate built-ins. Revisit if a page must be public but hidden in the app.
blocks.holds: Sync of built-in share rows in share-model

blocks.title: Wider call to action
blocks.body: Whether the page shows a general signup prompt as well as the edit prompt, and its wording and placement. edit-prompt builds only the Decision 10 prompt.
blocks.options: None in v1, or a small extra job before launch.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: leave it out of the v1 jobs, and add one small job if you want it before the link goes on the marketing site.

blocks.title: Error monitoring
blocks.body: New in this plan. The public entry does not load main.tsx, so it gets no Datadog RUM, and `DataDogRum` comes from the `@calctree/editor` root, which the page must not import. Without a choice, nobody sees errors on public pages. entry-shrink routes base-editor's direct Datadog imports through a reporter, so the public entry can plug in whichever option you choose.
blocks.options: None in v1. RUM started by the public entry (check its cookie settings first). PostHog exception capture (check that the installed posthog-js 1.250.2 supports it).
blocks.rec: Decide at checkpoint A. No job depends on it.

blocks.title: Host for user links
blocks.body: Added 2026-11-13. Decision 13 put `/t/<slug>` on the app host when only staff could publish. With sharing, any author can put content on that origin, where the app keeps a signed-in user's tokens in localStorage (`token-store.ts:65-71`), and the content can carry links.
blocks.options: Keep the app host. Or a second hostname on the same distribution, where a CloudFront Function serves only the public paths (share-host). Not verified: whether the certificate and distribution take a second name without a new distribution.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: the second hostname, before any non-staff user can make a link public.

blocks.title: Which version a share shows
blocks.body: Added 2026-11-13. A template gets new versions; Claude's link always shows the latest. The gate for "Anyone with the link" needs a browser run, so the server cannot update a public page on its own.
blocks.options: Always the latest. Or pinned at share time. Or latest for the two signed-in levels and pinned for the public link.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: the latest for "Only you" and "Anyone in the workspace"; the public link stays on the version that passed the gate, and the dialog offers "Update to v<n>".

blocks.title: What "Only you" hides
blocks.body: Added 2026-11-13. Every member sees every workspace template in the template gallery today (`workspaceTemplateRepo.ts:286-302`). In Claude, private means nobody else sees the item at all.
blocks.options: The level controls the link only. Or "Only you" also hides the template from other members' gallery, which needs owner-filtered sync.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: the link only, and the dialog says so.

blocks.title: Who may make links public
blocks.body: Added 2026-11-13. Claude showed "Anyone with the link" disabled under an organisation setting.
blocks.options: Everyone. Paid plans only. A workspace setting that lets Admins turn the public level off.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: roll out behind a feature flag; the plan question is a product call.

blocks.title: Abuse handling
blocks.body: Added 2026-11-13. With sharing, anyone who can author a template can publish content on a CalcTree host: a phishing page, or a page that hits a future flaw in the view.
blocks.options: Staff takedown. A report link on the public page. Both. Neither for v1.
blocks.rec: My suggestion: both. share-writer has the takedown and public-share-shell the report link, unless you say otherwise.

blocks.title: Visitor URL
blocks.body: `/t/<slug>` on the app host. A CloudFront Function rewrites `/t/*` to `/public-template.html`.

blocks.title: Data URL
blocks.body: `/public-templates/<slug>/page.json`, from its own bucket, with `cache-control: max-age=60`. Publish and unpublish both invalidate `/public-templates/<slug>/*`, because the distribution caches a missing page.json as the app HTML for 5 minutes (https://github.com/calctree/frontend/pull/4345).

blocks.title: Slug
blocks.body: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. 1 to 63 characters, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

blocks.title: page.json v1
blocks.body: Fields below. `values` is the same `Record<string, string>` that `runTemplatePreviewInBrowser` returns, and that `publishedValues` takes.

blocks.title: Not found
blocks.body: Any response that is not a page.json v1 is the not-found state. For a missing file, the CDN returns the app's HTML with status 200.

blocks.title: Analytics event
blocks.body: `public_template_edit_prompt_clicked`, with `slug` and `block_kind` (`python` or `formula`).

blocks.title: Share id (Milestone B)
blocks.body: The slug of a shared template: random, lowercase, at least 100 bits, and it fits the slug rule. One per template. Staff may give a built-in a readable slug. Added 2026-11-13.

blocks.title: Share levels (Milestone B)
blocks.body: `private` ("Only you": the author and workspace Admins), `workspace` ("Anyone in <workspace>": any member, Viewers included), `link` ("Anyone with the link": anyone, through the static page.json). Who can change it: the template's author (`workspace_templates.created_by`) or a workspace Admin, never a Viewer; staff with `can-manage-builtin-templates` for built-ins. Added 2026-11-13.

blocks.title: Share links (Milestone B)
blocks.body: The copied link is always `/t/<shareId>`. The public page draws it when page.json exists. Otherwise it offers sign-in to `/s/<shareId>`, the app route, which checks the level and the role. page.json may carry `indexable: true`, written for built-ins only; readers ignore fields they do not know. Added 2026-11-13.

Checkpoint A: publish the first link by hand
steps: Merge the Milestone A PRs, then deploy the editor-web stack and the app to staging.
Choose the launch template (open decision: launch set). Export its MDX and repeat spike (e) on it; the spike ran (e) only on a stand-in.

Build page.json with the snapshot-builder dev route, `/dev/public-template-snapshot/<workspaceId>` with `can-manage-builtin-templates` on (https://github.com/calctree/frontend/pull/4365). The PR says the route was never run in a browser, so this is its first end-to-end run. Read the warnings (`user-mention`, `internal-link`) before uploading.

Done on staging on 2026-11-12 for https://github.com/calctree/frontend/pull/4345: an anonymous read of a hand-uploaded page.json returns it with the locked-down headers; listing and anonymous writes fail; the `/t/` rewrite runs; a missing page.json returns the app HTML with the app headers. Repeat the read and the write checks on production after its deploy. The read check was done on production on 2026-11-13: a hand-uploaded page.json under a throwaway slug was served through CloudFront and drawn on `/t/<slug>`, then removed and invalidated. The listing and anonymous-write checks on production are still open.

Upload it: `aws s3 cp page.json s3://<PublicTemplatesBucketName output>/public-templates/<slug>/page.json --content-type application/json --cache-control max-age=60 --profile staging`. If the URL was opened before the upload, invalidate `/public-templates/<slug>/*`, or wait 5 minutes.
Open `/t/<slug>` on staging as a signed-out visitor.
Check print preview in Safari, and check mobile Safari and in-app browsers (LinkedIn, Slack). CI covers none of these.
In real Safari on a Mac, time five cold Python starts. Docker WebKit stalled 18 of about 60 starts at 26-38 s against 7-10 s. If real Safari stalls too, it needs a job before the link goes public.
Confirm that stored values show within 2 s on a throttled 10 Mbit/s link with 50 ms RTT.
Decide error monitoring before the link goes on the marketing site.
Repeat on production. Then decide whether Milestone B starts.

blocks.title: Checkpoint B: sharing on staging
steps: Decide the five sharing decisions first: host for user links, which version a share shows, what "Only you" hides, who may make links public, and abuse handling.
Deploy publish-iam, then pages with share-model and share-writer, then redeploy the mesh so the gateway has the new fields.
If you chose a second hostname, deploy share-host and check it with curl.
Merge and deploy share-viewer, public-share-shell, share-dialog and shares-list, with the share flag on for staff only.

On staging, with three accounts (the author, a member, an outsider) and a signed-out browser, walk one template through all three levels with the same link, and check each cell of the access table in the Sharing section.
Move a public share back to "Only you" and time the not-public state against 10 minutes.
Repeat on production, then decide the rollout of the flag.

blocks.title: Definition of done
items: `/t/<slug>` shows the template's prose and calculation blocks with the published values to a visitor with no cookies and no account, before Python has finished starting, and within 2 s on a 10 Mbit/s link with 50 ms RTT.
Changing an input recalculates in the browser and updates dependent outputs, for a template with at least one MathJS and one Python statement.
While Python is starting, MathJS outputs that do not depend on Python update at once. Python-dependent outputs show a computing state.
A value that references another template variable runs and the field stays editable. A circular value is refused at its input, and the last good values stay.
"Reset to published values" restores every input and the published outputs.
During a whole session (load, input changes, print), the browser makes no request to mesh, pages, calculations, datasets, samantha, rudi or Gutenberg. A Playwright test fails on any such request.
Two browser contexts on the same slug with different inputs show independent values.
A value with a different dimension from its published value is refused with a message. A compatible unit is accepted. Never a silent wrong value.
A statement that fails shows an error on the page, not a blank output.
Python runs in a dedicated Worker. A script still running after 30 s is stopped: the worker restarts, a message shows, and the last good values stay.
Print gives a paginated document with the visitor's current values and a Python plot, with no call to Gutenberg.

The public module graph has none of the forbidden modules (now including Datadog RUM and fast-check, with posthog-js only in a lazy chunk) and stays within the gzip budget from entry-shrink. A bundle test fails the build.
Python code and derived formulas are read-only. A click shows "Edit the formulas and code in CalcTree", opens signup, and is recorded.
Only a user with `can-manage-builtin-templates` can mark a built-in version public or unpublish it. Built-ins are never public by default.
Publishing refuses a version with `<Dataset>` or `<PageFiles>`, with `needsServer: true`, with any statement error, or with values that differ from the server's at the pinned revision.
After unpublish, the page shows its not-found state within 10 minutes.

(Milestone B, 2026-11-13) The template's author or a workspace Admin can set its share to "Only you", "Anyone in the workspace" or "Anyone with the link". Other members and Viewers cannot, and the API refuses them.
(Milestone B) A template has one share link, `/t/<shareId>`, and it does not change when the level changes.

(Milestone B) At "Anyone in the workspace", a signed-in member who opens the link sees the template and can change its inputs. A signed-in non-member sees the no-access page. A signed-out visitor sees a sign-in prompt and none of the content.
(Milestone B) At "Only you", only the author and workspace Admins can open the link.
(Milestone B) "Anyone with the link" can be chosen only when the publish gate passes. Otherwise the option is disabled and the gate's reasons are shown.
(Milestone B) Moving a share away from "Anyone with the link" removes public access within 10 minutes.
(Milestone B) A list shows the shares the user can open, with their level, and can show only the user's own.

blocks.title: Re-run the anonymous public-page spike on current main in three browsers
blocks.goal: Answer seven questions with measurements before any production code exists, and give a go or no-go against criteria written in advance.
blocks.note: Done: https://github.com/calctree/frontend/pull/4343 (draft, do not merge). GO, with entry-shrink added for the throttled load. (e) still needs a real built-in export.
scope: Start a new branch from origin/main, for example `spike/public-template-pages-rerun`. Copy the spike files by path (`git checkout origin/spike/public-template-pages -- <paths>`) from https://github.com/calctree/frontend/pull/4318. All ten are new files that main has not touched, so the copy reverts nothing on main. The files: `apps/editor-web/spike.html`, `apps/editor-web/src/spike-main.tsx`, `apps/editor-web/scripts/spike-print-capture.mjs`, `packages/calculations/src/useCalculation/publicPage.spike.test.ts`, `packages/editor/spike-bundle.vite.config.ts`, `packages/editor/spike-print-entry.ts`, `packages/editor/spike-print.vite.config.ts`, `packages/editor/spike-public-entry.ts`, `packages/editor/src/spike/PublicTemplatePageSpike.tsx` and `packages/editor/src/spike/README.md`.

(a) Run MathJS and Python anonymously, with Python in a dedicated Worker (the spike page takes `?worker=dedicated`). Count CalcTree requests in Playwright Chromium, WebKit and Firefox. editor-web's `playwright.config.ts` has only a chromium project, so add the other two on this branch.
(b) Draw the page from a hand-made values map before the engine starts, through `publishedValues` or a serialized `emittedValue`.
(c) Time the Python start on a cold load and on a reload, with the full package list and with the PyPI (micropip) list removed.
(d) During the Python start, run a MathJS-only pass. Check that MathJS outputs update and that statements reading Python outputs fail as undefined names.

(e) Use the MDX of one existing built-in version with a Python plot and no `<Dataset>` or `<PageFiles>`. Check that it renders and prints with the plot. Run (e) first on the stand-in `packages/templates/src/page-templates/stressStrainCurve.ts` (Python with matplotlib, no `<Dataset>` or `<PageFiles>`). That file is a New page banner template, not a built-in version, so label the result as a stand-in. Adam will supply a real built-in export; repeat (e) on it when it arrives.
(f) Put a circular reference through a Python statement. Record whether the run rejects or returns errors.
(g) Build the public entry with Vite and record the gzipped size. Propose the budget for the bundle test in public-entry.
Time box: two days.
Deliverable: a draft PR with "(do not merge)" in its title. Its body holds a results table (question, number, browser, commit) and the go or no-go verdict.
out: Pushing to `spike/public-template-pages`. It is dpnova's branch, and a rebase there would need a force push.
Commenting on other PRs. Adam decides where the results go.
accept: Each of (a) to (g) has a measured answer, or a stated reason it could not be measured.

The PR body states go or no-go against the plan's criteria, written before the run: go if all three engines make zero CalcTree requests, recompute in under 1 s once warm, and show stored values within 2 s of navigation on a cold load.

If Python does not run in one engine, stop and raise a client_decision blocker. The options are to drop Python templates from the launch set, or to show stored values with a "not supported in this browser" note on Python outputs.
